A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Safe Exploration via Policy Priors and retain the main paper and Appendices A–G. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support reliable comparison despite revised proofs and pagination.

before.justification: v3 reports original control and navigation experiments, real race-car learning results, and appendix ablations and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix D, including simulation, vision-control and real-hardware experiments.

M1.justification: Equation (9) changes the expansion bonus weight from gamma^(t/2) to gamma^t, giving exploration and expansion bonuses the same temporal discount. Corresponding objectives in Lemma 12 and Appendix C are updated. This modifies the retained SOOPER objective without adding a component; the PDFs do not establish a changed experimental implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RWRL, SafetyGym and RaceCar tasks, including vision control, offline-to-online learning, real hardware, goal-size transfer and action-noise scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: SAILR, CRPO and Primal-Dual in the main comparisons, with braking/from-scratch variants, SafeCRPO and Log Barriers retained in the appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: Empirical protocols retain the default 128 evaluation trajectories, undiscounted reward/cost metrics, data budgets, vision inputs and domain-randomization ranges in Tables 1–2. The revised truncation horizon appears in the regret proof, not as a reported experimental protocol change.

E4.justification: Appendix D retains the same analyses of initialization, terminations, prior conservatism, action noise, pessimism, optimism/regret, direct cost-based learning and runtime. Figure relocation does not add or remove an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five-seed design, means and standard errors for hardware experiments, and means and standard deviations for runtime. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The empirical result entries and findings are retained. Corresponding plots in Figures 3, 5–6 and 8–17 contain identical curves, bars and uncertainty displays; neither revised performance values nor additional results are reported.

T1.justification: Section 3 removes Lipschitz continuity of epistemic uncertainty, adds a bounded-density condition for the optimal policy, and specifies a truncated-Gaussian safe prior. Appendix A substantially rewrites the safety induction using conditional expectations and explicit absorbing fallback. Appendix B replaces Lemma 7's Gaussian-difference argument with an action-density change-of-measure proof, changes the safety-gap definition to include histories, and revises downstream constants, discount factors and the truncation horizon. The final asymptotic regret order is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same headline claims of safety throughout learning, convergence and sublinear cumulative regret, scalability, and strong empirical performance. No main contribution is added or removed.

C2.justification: The theoretical applicability conditions change through the new policy-density restrictions and removal of the uncertainty-Lipschitz requirement. Appendix D also drops its specific attribution of Gaussian-noise dependence to Lemma 7. Interpretations of empirical results and the conclusion's stated future-work limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The practical implementation description, prior-training recipes, hardware information, data-processing details and domain-randomization parameters are retained. The new policy distribution requirements are formal assumptions rather than newly reported implementation settings; access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Vignola et al. (2026), Sampling-based safe reinforcement learning, citing its martingale lemma in the cumulative-regret proof. Section 2's research positioning and the remaining cited-work membership are unchanged.

P1.justification: Explanatory prose surrounding the safety proof and Lemma 7 is rewritten and expanded, with localized edits to the problem setting and proof overview. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing appendix displays are repositioned: Figure 8 moves from page 33 to 34, Figure 17 from page 38 to 39, and Figure 7's text wrapping changes. All 19 figures and both tables are retained without changed plot contents or table structures.

improvement.justification: v4 improves theoretical precision: Lemma 7 supplies an explicit density-ratio derivation under stated additional assumptions, Appendix A clarifies conditioning and fallback behavior, and Equation (9) aligns with the revised discounting analysis. These make important proof dependencies easier to assess. The gain is qualified by more restrictive policy requirements and unchanged empirical support; it does not establish broader applicability or complete resolution of the theoretical guarantees.
